findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator negative-offset path crashes on Django QuerySet
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result the branch for `cursor.offset < 0` does `list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset < 0`. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ explicitly raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` for any negative start or stop in a slice. The comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is wrong; OffsetPaginator in the same file even guards against this with `raise BadPaginationError('Pagination offset cannot be negative')`. Consequence: any caller of the new endpoint that supplies a negative `cursor.offset` (the entire advertised feature) crashes instead of paginating. Since `optimized_pagination=true` is gated to superusers / `has_global_access`, this is a privilege-escalation-free DoS for admins and a broken feature for everyone else.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM aggregation mangles timestamps used as eviction scores
findings.body: The new eviction relies on scores being `end_timestamp_precise` so that `ZPOPMIN ... COUNT (span_count - 1000)` evicts the oldest spans. But the unions use `zunionstore(set_key, 2, set_key, ...)` with the default `AGGREGATE` (SUM). Whenever a payload exists in both source keys (for example when `set_span_id == span_id`, making `set_key == span_key`, or any future overlap), the resulting score is `score1 + score2` instead of the timestamp. Doubling/adding scores corrupts the relative ordering used for eviction: older spans can end up with higher scores than newer ones, and `zpopmin` will then evict the wrong (newer) spans. The script should pass `AGGREGATE MAX` (or `MIN`) so the score remains a real timestamp.

findings.title: Redirect-chain iteration limit cut 10x without justification
findings.body: The for-loop bound is reduced from `10000` to `1000`. The removed comment explicitly warned: 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' Now any trace whose redirect chain exceeds depth 1000 will be truncated, causing spans to be written to the wrong `set_key`. The flushed segment will then be missing spans (data loss) or span sets will never reach their root timeout (resource leak / stuck segments). The PR description does not explain why a 10x tightening of this safety limit is safe, and no test covers deep chains.

findings.title: Unconditional dict access on end_timestamp_precise breaks older payloads
findings.body: `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` will raise `KeyError` for any Kafka payload that lacks the field. Older ingest-spans producers / relay versions, malformed messages, or any schema drift will now crash `process_batch` instead of being logged-and-skipped, because the prior code did not require this key. Either guard with `val.get("end_timestamp_precise")` (and default to e.g. `0.0` or the message timestamp) or reject the payload explicitly with a metric. As written this is a silent backwards-compatibility break for every span that does not carry the new field.

findings.title: max_segment_spans guard removed in Python but constructor arg retained
findings.body: The `max_segment_spans` enforcement in `_load_segment_data` (the `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` block) has been deleted on the premise that Lua now evicts at insert time. The constructor parameter `max_segment_spans: int = 1001` is still accepted, still passed through `__reduce__`/`__init__`, but is no longer referenced anywhere in the module. There is no test that exercises the >1000 span eviction, and no Python-side safety net if the Lua script ever fails to load / evict (e.g. transient Redis script-cache miss or future regression). Either remove the dead parameter or keep a Python guard with a test.

findings.title: No test for the new >1000-span zpopmin eviction path
findings.body: test_buffer.py and test_flusher.py only add `end_timestamp_precise` to existing fixtures; nothing exercises a segment exceeding the 1000-element eviction threshold in add-buffer.lua, the `zunionstore`-score overlap case, or the new 1000-iteration redirect-chain limit. Given the eviction is the entire motivation for this PR and the only data-integrity-affecting change, the absence of a regression test means a broken eviction will not be caught by CI.
